title: The ordinary clopen composite localizes to the specified derived composite
statement: For a finite commutative ring Λ and a commutative proper/open square k,r,p,i of schemes, with k and i quasi-compact open immersions and r and p proper, the termwise exact localization derivedAlpha of the ordinary beta/projector/compositor word alpha equals properOpenAlpha. There is no cartesian, separatedness or finite-type hypothesis on this square. Definitions and operations are those of [def-sf-ambient-underived-clopen-comparison], [def-sf-ambient-exact-clopen-data], [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate].

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), map normalization; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change), adjunction transpose. Agent exact-localization comparison for the stated ambient categories; returned proof Step 6.

proof.text:
Localize the beta, clopen projection and the outgoing normalized compositors.
The beta equality follows from its definition as the localized ordinary isomorphism.
For the clopen projection, localize the reverse sheaf adjunction and use the exact
unit formula and the exact/direct-derived identification. The open compositor is
characterized by the composite Hom bijection; localization preserves that bijection.
The pullback compositor is the standard exact composition comparison. Exact-derived
transformation pasting combines these equalities, and transport by the total/exact
pullback isomorphisms gives the stated formula.

theorem ordinary_alpha_localized
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    {U V W Z : Scheme.{u}} (k : U ⟶ V) (r : U ⟶ W) (p : V ⟶ Z) (i : W ⟶ Z)
    [IsOpenImmersion k] [IsOpenImmersion i] [QuasiCompact k] [QuasiCompact i]
    [IsProper r] [IsProper p] (h : k ≫ p = r ≫ i) :
    derivedAlpha Λ k r p i h = properOpenAlpha Λ k r p i h
